title: Values at Written Indices
statement: Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $d,j,i\in\mathbb{N}$, with $i<j$. After writing the first $j$ values of $f$ into $\mu$ starting at $d$, the value at index $d+i$ is $f(i)$.
replaced:
Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and let $d,j,i\in\mathbb{N}$ with $i<j$. Define a
function by replacing $\mu(a)$ with $f(a-d)$ for indices $a$ in the interval $d\le
a<d+j$. Its value at $d+i$ is $f(i)$.
